messages:
Asha (marketing): Quick sync: we need a sharper set of competitive battlecards for the May webinar and the benchmark blog. Goal: sales can pick a 1-pager per competitor and route leads automatically. Short timeline.
Diego (gTM): Sounds good. Focus competitors: Cloud managed endpoints (AWS SageMaker/Vertex AI), LLM API providers (OpenAI/Anthropic), and infra/tooling vendors (Replicate, Lambda Labs, Databricks). Primary buyer signals: SLA requests, on-prem/air-gap, and cost complaints.
Priya (content): I'll draft two stylistic variants: "data-first" (benchmarks & numbers) and "playbook-first" (objections + scripts). Want to keep each card to ~6 bullets + one-line play for SDRs.
Liam (sales-eng): Must include: "Top sales trigger", "Top technical concern", "Script (30s)", "Escalation path". Example objection we see: "We already run on Vertex; it's easier for us."
Priya (content): Example script draft for Vertex/Cloud endpoints:
``` 
Objection: "We're on Vertex / SageMaker for managed endpoints."
30s script: "Vertex is great for training and broad model availability. If your app needs deterministic tail latency and predictable per-token economics at scale, Redwood Dedicated + prefix/KV caching cuts variance and unit cost. We also let you pin model versions and do canary rollouts without infra changes."
Deal signal: mentions latency variance, frequent model version drift.
Route: AE-enterprise + Solutions-eng.
```
Rina (product): For the benchmark blog — we can publish a standard microbenchmark: 512-token context, 1 warm prompt + 100 concurrent streams, median + p95 latency, and cost-per-1k-tokens on our Dedicated profile vs managed endpoints. Legal note: no direct price comparisons vs named competitors without sign-off.
Liam (sales-eng): For infra vendors (self-hosted): objection: "We like full control; we don't want managed services." 15s script: "Totally get it. Teams that choose Redwood keep control over model versions and quantization settings, but offload the operational burden: consistent benchmarks across GPUs, automatic batching, and rollout tooling. We also support private deployments if you need air-gapped installs."
Priya (content): Routing play snippet for inbound leads (we'll wire to Intercom/HubSpot):
``` 
if text contains ["latency", "p95", "SLA"]: tag -> "latency_sla" -> route AE-enterprise
if text contains ["on-prem", "air-gap", "airgapped", "private deployment"]: tag -> "onprem" -> route Solutions-Eng + AE
if text contains ["cost", "price per token", "pricing"]: tag -> "pricing" -> route SDR + pricing-sheet link
if text mentions competitor names ["OpenAI","Vertex","SageMaker","Replicate"]: add tag "comp:{name}" -> route to AE depending on tier
```
Diego (gTM): Nice. For the battlecards, add a compact "why we win" line and a single technical proof point (e.g., KV cache reduces repeated prefix cost by X% in our tests). Keep it punchy.
Asha (marketing): Agree. Priya, can you put the following structure on each card? - one-line positioning vs competitor - 3 bullet differentiators (product + ROI) - 2 example objections + 30s scripts - lead routing rule - 1 proof datapoint - owner (who to escalate to)
Priya (content): On it. I'll populate OpenAI, Anthropic, Vertex, Replicate, Databricks.
Liam: Add a "tech checklist" box for Solutions-eng: items like GPU types supported, quantization options, private deployment checklist, expected throughput, and common perf regressions.
Rina (product): I'll expose the microbenchmark harness and give Priya numbers by Monday. Also: we should avoid absolute claims like "X% cheaper" — use relative phrasing unless infra approves.
Diego (gTM): Can we A/B test two card variants in sales enablement? One with technical jargon, one with plain-language benefits. Track conversion to meeting over next 4 weeks.
Asha (marketing): Yes — owners: Priya (cards/content), Liam (sales objections list), Diego (routing rules + tracking), Rina (benchmarks). Deadline: card drafts by Friday EOD (1712016000). Final ship before webinar (1712630400).
ops-bot: Created doc: https://drive.redwood/marketing/battlecards/may-drafts (permissions: marketing/view).
Asha (marketing): Perfect. Quick ask: include a short webinar CTA in the footer + a single handler for folks who drop in saying "we want pricing" -> immediate SDR follow-up with pricing packet. Everyone OK with that?
Liam (sales-eng): Yep.
Diego (gTM): Good.
Priya (content): I'll include a footer template with CTA + routing links.
Rina (product): I'll send the benchmark caveats doc to legal.
Asha (marketing): Great work team. We'll reconvene Tue review (1712020000). :rocket:
